subtitle: Every kind of passive, and turning a clause round
words.intro: In the port of Hamburg, nobody loses a container. *Ein Container ist abhandengekommen*. Mistakes *wurden gemacht*. There are many ways to say so in German, and each of them is careful about who should be phoned.

grammar[0].blocks[1].root.q: Can you add gerade or a date for the action?
grammar[0].blocks[2].title: worden, not geworden
grammar[0].blocks[2].text: In the perfect passive: *Er ist festgenommen worden.*
grammar[0].fact: Passive with *werden* shows the action: *Das Tor wird geschlossen*. Passive with *sein* shows the result: *Das Tor ist geschlossen*. In English both can be *is closed*, and that’s where your signs get confusing. A shop that *wird geschlossen* may be going out of business.

grammar[1].subheading: Where the verb goes, the same subject, and special shapes
grammar[1].blocks[0].title: Where the verb goes
grammar[1].blocks[1].note: A new subject keeps the clause: Er sprach langsam, damit man ihn verstand.
grammar[1].blocks[2].title: Special shapes
grammar[1].fact: German lets you choose how a clause is joined to the next: *Nachdem er kam*, *nach seiner Ankunft*, *Kaum war er da*. Each one is a little faster than the last. In the very best German prose, the fastest form appears just as things start to go wrong.

document.intro: A real waybill. A chest is being shipped by a carter, *in göttlicher Begleitung*, in God’s company, and the printed form says so. There’s a line for the goods.
document.fact: *Der Höchste verhelff’s in salvo*, says the form: may the Almighty bring it safely. It’s printed. So they had a standard form for hoping, and it took up more space than the goods.
document.tasks[1].instruction: Say each one in the passive.
reading.intro: Remember Max’s wardrobe? He sold it on the internet, to a buyer in Valparaíso. Six weeks ago it was put on a ship at Hamburg. Now it’s gone. Max is at the shipping office, with Frau Huber, who only came to see the harbour. Herr Petersen behind the counter has been in the job for 34 years.
reading.fact: Hamburg is one of Europe’s largest container ports, with its huge cranes, ships and automated terminal. The city’s real love is the harbour. A very few containers really are lost each year, most of them at sea.
reading.tasks[1].instruction: Say each without saying who did it.
